questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Anjali said, 'He is the only son of my mother's only daughter's son.' How is the man related to Anjali?
questions.explanation: Anjali's mother's only daughter = Anjali (assuming Anjali has no sisters). So 'my mother's only daughter's son' = Anjali's son. The man is the only son of Anjali's son = Anjali's grandson.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A is the daughter of B, B is the son of C, and D is the wife of B, how is D related to A?
questions.explanation: B is A's father. D is B's wife ⟹ D is A's mother.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: From a point P, A walks 3 km East, 4 km North, and 3 km West. How far is A from P?
questions.explanation: Net E-W: 3 − 3 = 0. Net N-S: 4 km North. Distance = 4 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: From point P, B walks 8 km East, 6 km North, and 4 km West. Find PB.
questions.explanation: Net E-W: 8 − 4 = 4 km East. Net N: 6 km. Distance = √(4² + 6²) = √52 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All cricketers are athletes. All athletes are healthy.

Conclusions: I. All cricketers are healthy. II. Some healthy people are cricketers.
questions.explanation: Both follow by direct subset chain.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: No vegetable is a fruit. Some fruits are sweet.

Conclusions: I. No vegetable is sweet. II. Some sweet things are not vegetables.
questions.explanation: I: No-vegetable-is-fruit + some-fruits-sweet does NOT imply no-vegetable-is-sweet (vegetables could still be sweet via other means). FALSE. II: Some fruits are sweet; fruits ≠ vegetables ⟹ those sweet fruits are not vegetables. TRUE.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A < B = C and C ≥ D, which is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanation: A < B = C ≥ D. C ≥ D could mean C = D or C > D. So no strict relation between A and D — A could be less than, equal to, or greater than D. Cannot determine.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six students sit in a row. P is at one end. Q is to the immediate right of R. S is to the right of Q but to the left of T. P is to the right of T. The order from left:
options: U, R, Q, S, T, P
R, Q, S, T, P, U
U, S, R, Q, T, P
P, T, S, Q, R, U
questions.explanation: Constraints: P at right end (assume), R-Q adjacent (Q right of R), S right of Q & left of T, P right of T. Sequence: ...R, Q, S, ..., T, P. With 6 people, position U at left end. Order: U, R, Q, S, T, P. ✓
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 1 March 2024 is Friday, what day was 1 March 2023?
questions.explanation: 2023 was not leap year. From Mar 1, 2023 to Mar 1, 2024 = 366 days (Feb 29, 2024 falls in this range). 366 mod 7 = 2. Going BACK 2 days from Friday = Wednesday.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Question: Who is the youngest among A, B, C, D?

Statement I: B is younger than A and C.
Statement II: D is older than B.
questions.explanation: From I: B < A, B < C. From II: B < D. Combined: B is younger than A, C, D ⟹ B is youngest. Both together sufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which segment has led India's EV transition?
questions.passage_context: The future of mobility in India is being reshaped by electric vehicles. Government incentives, falling battery costs, and growing environmental awareness have all contributed to rapid EV adoption. Two-wheelers and three-wheelers have led the transition, accounting for the bulk of EV sales. Electric cars are slowly catching up, with major manufacturers launching competitive models. Charging infrastructure remains a key challenge — though the network has expanded significantly, gaps persist on highways and in smaller cities. Battery manufacturing is being scaled domestically through the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, reducing import dependence. If sustained, the EV transition could reduce India's oil import bill, improve urban air quality, and create new manufacturing jobs.
questions.explanation: Stated explicitly: 'Two-wheelers and three-wheelers have led the transition.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:
Rearrange and identify the FIRST sentence.

(A) Today, hundreds of millions of Indians use it daily.
(B) UPI was launched in 2016 by NPCI.
(C) Initially limited to a few partner banks, it scaled rapidly.
(D) Cross-border integrations are now being explored.
(E) The next phase will likely focus on global UPI partnerships.
questions.explanation: B (intro: UPI launch) → C (rapid scaling) → A (current scale) → D (cross-border) → E (closing). 1st = B.
questions.subject: ENGLISH

questions.stem:

(A) The Indian middle class is rapidly growing.
(B) Higher disposable incomes have transformed consumption patterns.
(C) Domestic brands and international players compete fiercely.
(D) Online retail has expanded the choice further.
(E) The next decade will see continued evolution of consumer markets.
questions.explanation: A (growth) → B (impact) → C (competition) → D (online) → E (closing). Last = E.
